items.title: Not a secret
items.story: A classmate says this note is 'encrypted'. Is it?
items.hint: The text uses only A–Z, a–z, 0–9, + and /, and ends with =. Which encoding looks like that?
items.solution: It is Base64. Decode it: `base64 -d note.txt` (Linux) or CyberChef → From Base64. Base64 is an encoding, not encryption: anyone can reverse it.

items.title: Roman salad
items.story: An old message from Rome. The letters moved, but not very far.
items.hint: Each letter is shifted by the same number. There are only 25 shifts to try.
items.solution: Caesar cipher with shift 7. Shift every letter back by 7 (or try all 25 shifts in CyberChef → ROT13 with a custom amount). Braces and underscores do not change.

items.title: Mirror hex
items.story: These numbers look like hex. But something is also upside down.
items.hint: First turn the hex into text. Then look at the order of the characters.
items.solution: Hex-decode (`xxd -r -p data.txt`) to get the flag written backwards, then reverse it (`rev`).

items.title: Who can run it?
items.story:
Your server shows this file:

    -rwxr-x--x 1 root staff 8432 Oct 25 10:00 backup.sh

The flag is the permissions in octal, like ICO{644}.
items.hint: Split into three groups: owner, group, others. r = 4, w = 2, x = 1.
items.solution: Owner rwx = 4+2+1 = 7, group r-x = 4+1 = 5, others --x = 1. So the flag is ICO{751}.

items.title: Shout to everyone
items.story: A host has the address 192.168.37.70/27. What is the broadcast address of its subnet? Flag format: ICO{a.b.c.d}
items.hint: /27 means 32 − 27 = 5 host bits, so each subnet has 32 addresses.
items.solution: Subnets of size 32 in the last byte start at 0, 32, 64, 96… 70 is in 64–95. The broadcast address is the last one: 192.168.37.95. Flag ICO{192.168.37.95}.

items.title: Nothing to see here
items.story: The school club's new web page looks empty. The developer says it is finished.

files.name: index.html
files.content:
Welcome to the Cyber Club

Page coming soon.

items.hint: What the browser shows is not everything that is in the file.
items.solution: Open the file in a text editor or use View Source (Ctrl+U). The flag is in an HTML comment.

items.title: Magic numbers
items.story: Someone renamed a picture to report.docx to hide it. Here are its first bytes. What kind of file is it really? Flag format: ICO{extension}, lower case.
items.hint: Files start with 'magic bytes' that tell their real type. The `file` command uses them.
items.solution: 89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A is the PNG signature (you can even read 'PNG'). A real .docx would start with 50 4B (PK, a zip). Flag ICO{png}.

items.title: Night shift
items.story: The web server log from last night. One address guessed passwords until it got in. Flag format: ICO{ip address}

items.title: One key to rule them
items.story: This was XOR-encrypted with a key that is only one byte long.
items.hint: A one-byte key has only 256 options. You also know the plaintext starts with 'ICO{'.
items.solution: XOR the first byte (0x63) with 'I' (0x49) to get the key 0x2a. XOR every byte with 0x2a (CyberChef: From Hex → XOR key 2a).

items.title: The French square
items.story: Like Caesar, but the shift changes with each letter. The key is LEVEL.
items.hint: Vigenère: letter n is shifted by key letter n (A = 0, B = 1 …). Only letters use up the key.
items.solution: Decrypt with key LEVEL (CyberChef → Vigenère Decode). Braces and underscores are skipped and do not use a key letter.

items.title: Check, please
items.story: This program says OK only for the right flag. Make it say OK.

files.name: checker.py

items.hint: Each character is XORed with a number that depends only on its position. XOR can be undone with the same number.
items.solution: For each position i, the character is chr(SECRET[i] ^ (i*7 % 256)). In Python: `''.join(chr(s ^ (i*7 % 256)) for i, s in enumerate(SECRET))`.

items.title: Cookie jar
items.story: You logged in to a test site and found this cookie. The developer thinks it is safe because it is 'signed'.
items.hint: The cookie has three parts separated by dots. That is a JWT.
items.solution: A JWT is header.payload.signature, each part Base64URL. Decode the middle part: the flag is in the 'note' field. Signing stops changes, it does not hide data.
